# 🚗 Spring Break Family Road Trip: Seattle → San Antonio → Austin → Houston
### April 10–18 | Family of 4 | Budget: $3,000

---

## 1. 🚙 Rental Car

### Recommendation: Mid-Size SUV (Toyota RAV4, Ford Escape, or similar)

A mid-size SUV is the sweet spot for your family — enough cargo space for 4 people's luggage, comfortable for highway miles, and better fuel economy than a full-size SUV.

**Why not a minivan?** Minivans offer more space but cost ~$30–50/day more and get worse fuel economy. For a 7-day trip with moderate luggage, a mid-size SUV is the better value.

**Estimated Cost: $420–$560 total**
- Daily rate: $55–$75/day × 8 days
- One-way drop fee (SAT → HOU/IAH): Often $0–$75 on this route since it's a common Texas corridor — confirm when booking
- Taxes/fees at airport: Add ~25–30% to quoted rate (airport surcharges are real — budget $100–$120 extra)

**Realistic all-in cost: $520–$680**

### 🏆 Best Rental Car Tips for This Route

| Tip | Details |
|-----|---------|
| **Book through Costco Travel or Costco Auto** | Members get pre-negotiated rates with no hidden fees — often 20–30% cheaper than booking direct |
| **Compare on AutoSlash.com** | Tracks price drops on existing reservations and finds coupon codes automatically |
| **Avoid airport add-ons at the counter** | Decline GPS (use your phone), prepaid fuel (you'll return it full), and PAI insurance (check your existing auto policy and credit card coverage first) |
| **Use a credit card with rental car coverage** | Chase Sapphire, Capital One Venture, and many others offer primary or secondary CDW coverage — read your card's terms before declining the rental company's insurance |
| **Book at SAT, drop at HOU (not IAH)** | William P. Hobby (HOU) is closer to downtown Houston and your flight departs from there — confirm your return flight is HOU vs. IAH |
| **Book early** | Spring Break is peak season in Texas — prices rise significantly in late March |

---

## 2. 🏨 Hotels

### San Antonio — 3 Nights (April 10–13)

**Spring Break note:** San Antonio hotels near the Riverwalk fill up fast and prices spike during Spring Break. Book immediately if you haven't already. Expect premium pricing of $150–$250/night for decent family rooms.

---

#### Option A: 🥇 Drury Plaza Hotel San Antonio Riverwalk *(Best Value Pick)*
**~$180–$210/night | ~$540–$630 for 3 nights**

| ✅ Pros | ❌ Cons |
|---------|---------|
| Legendary free hot breakfast included (saves $50–$80/day for a family of 4) | Rooms can sell out months in advance |
| Free "5:30 Kickback" with hot food + 3 free drinks each evening | Parking is $30–$35/night (valet) |
| Pool on-site | Not directly on the Riverwalk but 2-minute walk |
| Kids eat free with paying adult | Building is historic — elevators can be slow |
| Excellent TripAdvisor ratings consistently | |

**Why it's great for families:** The free breakfast and evening kickback alone can save your family $100+/day, which is massive for a budget-conscious trip. Kids love the food spread.

---

#### Option B: Hyatt Regency San Antonio Riverwalk
**~$220–$270/night | ~$660–$810 for 3 nights**

| ✅ Pros | ❌ Cons |
|---------|---------|
| Directly on the Riverwalk — walk out and you're there | More expensive |
| Beautiful pool area kids will love | Breakfast not included |
| Spacious rooms, good for families | Parking ~$40/night |
| Hyatt points if you're a member | Can feel chaotic during Spring Break |

**Why it's great for families:** Unbeatable location — you step off the elevator and you're at the river. Eliminates the need to drive anywhere for the first two evenings.

---

#### Option C: *(Budget-Friendly)* Hampton Inn San Antonio Riverwalk
**~$140–$175/night | ~$420–$525 for 3 nights**

| ✅ Pros | ❌ Cons |
|---------|---------|
| Free breakfast included | Less "wow factor" than the other options |
| Reliable, clean, family-proven brand | Pool may be small/crowded |
| Lower price point saves budget for activities | Short walk to Riverwalk (5–8 min) |
| Hilton Honors points | Standard hotel feel |

**💡 Recommendation:** Book the **Drury Plaza** — the free meals make it the best actual value even at a higher nightly rate.

---

### Austin — 4 Nights (April 13–17)

Austin during Spring Break is even more expensive than San Antonio. Budget hotel options near South Congress or downtown start around $150–$180/night.

---

#### Option A: 🥇 South Congress Hotel *(Best Experience Pick)*
**~$220–$280/night | ~$880–$1,120 for 4 nights**

| ✅ Pros | ❌ Cons |
|---------|---------|
| *On* South Congress Ave — walk to everything | Most expensive option |
| Stunning pool area kids will love | Can be noisy on weekends (SoCo is lively) |
| Excellent on-site restaurant | Parking $30–$35/night |
| Quintessentially Austin vibe | Boutique style — rooms vary in size |
| Walking distance to food trucks, shops | May exceed budget if combined with Drury |

**Why it's great for families:** You're walking distance from the best of Austin's food scene, shopping, and street life. Kids ages 8–11 will love exploring SoCo on foot.

---

#### Option B: Hyatt Place Austin Downtown
**~$170–$210/night | ~$680–$840 for 4 nights**

| ✅ Pros | ❌ Cons |
|---------|---------|
| Free breakfast included | Downtown Austin can have traffic/parking challenges |
| Walkable to 6th Street, Lady Bird Lake | Less "Austin character" — feels more corporate |
| Reliable family-friendly brand | Further from South Congress |
| Pool on-site | |

---

#### Option C: *(Budget-Friendly)* Fairfield Inn & Suites Austin South
**~$130–$160/night | ~$520–$640 for 4 nights**

| ✅ Pros | ❌ Cons |
|---------|---------|
| Lowest cost, free breakfast | Need to drive to most attractions |
| Suite-style rooms — separate living area great for kids | Less walkable |
| Pool, good parking | Generic suburban feel |
| Saves significant budget | |

**💡 Recommendation:** If budget allows, **South Congress Hotel** is a once-in-a-while experience worth the splurge. If you need to trim, **Hyatt Place Downtown** with free breakfast is the practical choice.

## 3. 📅 Day-by-Day Itinerary

### 🌮 SAN ANTONIO (April 10–13)

---

#### **April 10 (Thursday) — Arrival Day**
*Arriving afternoon — kids will be tired from flying*

| Time | Activity | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| Afternoon | Land at SAT, pick up rental car | Allow 45–60 min for car pickup — Spring Break lines can be long |
| ~4:00 PM | Check into hotel | Drop bags, let kids decompress for 30 min |
| ~5:30 PM | **Walk the Riverwalk** | Easy, low-energy, visually impressive — kids will be wowed |
| ~6:30 PM | **Dinner at Casa Rio** | Historic Riverwalk restaurant, family-friendly, outdoor seating over the water — an iconic first San Antonio meal |
| ~8:00 PM | Ice cream at **Haagen-Dazs on the Riverwalk** or **Marble Slab Creamery** | Perfect wind-down activity |
| ~8:30 PM | Back to hotel | Early night — everyone's on Pacific Time, it'll feel like 6:30 PM |

**💡 Tip:** Don't over-schedule arrival day. A walk + dinner + ice cream is the perfect low-key intro to the city.

---

#### **April 11 (Friday) — Full Day San Antonio**
*The Alamo + San Antonio Missions + Natural Bridge Caverns*

| Time | Activity | Cost (Family of 4) |
|------|----------|--------------------|
| 8:00 AM | Hotel breakfast | Included (Drury) |
| 9:00 AM | **The Alamo** | FREE — arrive early before crowds build |
| 10:30 AM | **San Antonio Missions National Historical Park** | FREE — drive the Mission Trail (4 missions, ~30 min total drive) |
| 12:30 PM | Lunch at **Mi Tierra Café** in Market Square | ~$40–$50 |
| 1:30 PM | **Market Square (El Mercado)** | Free to browse — great for kids to explore |
| 3:00 PM | **Natural Bridge Caverns** (30 min north of SA) | ~$100 for family of 4 — kids ages 8 & 11 will *love* this |
| 5:30 PM | Return to Riverwalk | |
| 6:30 PM | **Dinner at Boudro's Texas Bistro** or walk the river | ~$60–$80 |
| 8:00 PM | **Riverwalk evening stroll** — beautifully lit at night | Free |

---

#### **April 12 (Saturday) — Full Day San Antonio**
*SeaWorld or Six Flags + Dinner*

**Morning Option A (Recommended for ages 8 & 11): SeaWorld San Antonio**
- Opens at 10:00 AM, ~20 min from Riverwalk
- Cost: ~$50–$60/person if booked online in advance (skip gate pricing of $80+)
- **Family of 4: ~$180–$200**
- Kids this age are the *perfect* age for SeaWorld — big enough for all rides, still excited about animal shows

**Morning Option B: Six Flags Fiesta Texas**
- Great thrill rides for the 11-year-old especially
- Cost: ~$45–$55/person online advance
- **Family of 4: ~$160–$200**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 9:00 AM | Drive to SeaWorld/Six Flags |
| 10:00 AM–5:00 PM | Full day at park |
| 6:00 PM | **Dinner at The County Line BBQ** — classic Texas BBQ, kid-friendly |
| 7:30 PM | Final Riverwalk walk — last night in San Antonio |

---

#### **April 13 (Sunday) — Morning Before Checkout**
*Quick activity, then drive to Austin*

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 8:00 AM | Hotel breakfast |
| 9:00 AM | **San Antonio Zoo** — compact, excellent zoo, 2 hours is enough | ~$60 family of 4 |
| **OR** | **Brackenridge Park** — free outdoor park, great for kids to run around before a car ride | Free |
| 11:00 AM | Checkout, load car |
| 11:30 AM | Drive to Austin (I-35 N, ~1.5 hours) |
| 1:00 PM | Arrive Austin |

---

### 🎸 AUSTIN (April 13–17)

---

#### **April 13 (Sunday) — Arrival Afternoon**
*First evening in Austin — ease in, explore South Congress*

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 1:00 PM | Check into hotel (or drop bags if early) |
| 2:00 PM | **South Congress Ave walk** — browse the famous shops and street art |
| 3:30 PM | **Amy's Ice Creams** on South Congress | Austin institution — kids will love it |
| 4:30 PM | **Barton Springs Pool** (if warm enough) | $5–$9/person, spring-fed outdoor pool — iconic Austin experience |
| 7:00 PM | **Dinner at Hopdoddy Burger Bar** on South Congress | Family-friendly, excellent burgers, ~$50 |
| 8:30 PM | Walk back to hotel | |

---

#### **April 14 (Monday) — Full Day Austin**
*Outdoor Austin + Lady Bird Lake + Congress Ave Bats*

| Time | Activity | Cost |
|------|----------|------|
| 8:30 AM | Breakfast at **Juan in a Million** — legendary breakfast tacos | ~$25 |
| 10:00 AM | **Lady Bird Lake Kayak/Paddle Board rental** | ~$60–$80/hour for 2 kayaks — kids 8 & 11 can handle this easily |
| 12:00 PM | **Barton Creek Greenbelt** — swim in the natural swimming hole | Free |
| 2:00 PM | **Zilker Park** — kite flying, frisbee, picnic | Free |
| 4:00 PM | Rest at hotel |
| 7:30 PM | Walk to **Congress Avenue Bridge** for **bat watching** 🦇 | FREE — 1.5 million bats emerge at dusk. One of the most unique urban wildlife events in North America. Kids will *never* forget this. |
| 9:00 PM | Dinner near the bridge |

---

#### **April 15 (Tuesday) — Full Day Austin**
*Museums + Music + Food Trucks*

| Time | Activity | Cost |
|------|----------|------|
| 9:00 AM | **Bullock Texas State History Museum** | ~$40 family — engaging for ages 8 & 11, great IMAX theater |
| 11:30 AM | **Texas State Capitol** grounds tour | FREE — kids love climbing the steps and the rotunda |
| 1:00 PM | **South Congress Food Truck Park** for lunch | ~$30–$40 |
| 2:30 PM | **Blanton Museum of Art** (UT Campus) | $10 adults, kids free — check for family programs |
| 4:00 PM | **UT Austin campus walk** — Darrell K Royal Stadium, the Tower | Free |
| 6:30 PM | **Rainey Street** or **6th Street** for dinner | ~$60 |
| 8:00 PM | **Stubbs Amphitheater** outdoor area or live music on 6th St | Free or cheap — even just walking 6th Street with live music spilling out of every bar is a memorable Austin experience for kids |

---

#### **April 16 (Wednesday) — Full Day Austin**
*Day Trip or Theme/Water Park*

**Option A: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area** *(Highly Recommended)*
- 1.5 hours west of Austin in the Hill Country
- A massive pink granite dome you can climb — stunning views
- Kids 8 & 11 will absolutely love this hike
- **Cost:** $8/person day use = $32 for family
- **Reserve a timed entry pass in advance at recreation.gov** — it fills up, especially Spring Break
- Pack snacks and water

**Option B: Austin Aquarium**
- Good rainy-day alternative
- ~$25/person, family of 4 = ~$90
- Less impressive than major aquariums but solid for kids

**Option C: Schlitterbahn New Braunfels Water Park**
- 45 min from Austin (toward San Antonio)
- One of the top-rated water parks in the country
- ~$60–$70/person = ~$240 for family
- Only if weather is warm (Texas in April can be 80s°F — likely yes)

| Evening | Activity |
|---------|----------|
| 7:00 PM | **Final Austin dinner at Uchi or Torchy's Tacos** — Torchy's is kid-friendly, creative tacos, ~$40 |
| 8:30 PM | Stroll South Congress one last time |

---

#### **April 17 (Thursday) — Checkout + Drive to Houston**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 8:00 AM | Breakfast at hotel or **Tacodeli** (breakfast tacos — Austin staple) |
| 9:00 AM | Checkout, load car |
| 9:30 AM | **Drive Austin → Houston** (I-10 East, ~2.5 hours) |
| 10:30 AM | Optional stop: **Buc-ee's in Luling, TX** — the kids NEED to experience this. The world's largest gas station/travel plaza. It's genuinely a tourist attraction. |
| 12:00–1:00 PM | Arrive Houston |
| Afternoon | **Houston option:** Space Center Houston (~$100 family) or just check in, relax, prep for morning flight |
| Evening | Dinner in Houston — **Pappadeaux Seafood** or **Goode Company BBQ** |

## 5. 🗺️ Driving Routes

### San Antonio (SAT) → Austin
- **Route:** I-35 North — it's the only practical highway option
- **Distance:** ~80 miles
- **Drive Time:** 1.5–2 hours (allow 2 hours during Spring Break — traffic through San Marcos can be slow on weekends)
- **Worth stopping:**
  - **San Marcos, TX** (halfway point): Home to **Texas State University** campus on the beautiful San Marcos River. If kids need to stretch, **Sewell Park** on the river is a quick, beautiful stop. Also: **Prime Outlets San Marcos** if you want to shop.
  - **New Braunfels, TX:** The **Guadalupe River** flows through here — gorgeous Hill Country scenery on the bridge over the river.

### Austin → Houston (HOU Airport)
- **Route:** I-10 East to TX-99 South (Grand Parkway) to HOU, **OR** direct I-10 to US-59 South to HOU
- **Distance:** ~165 miles
- **Drive Time:** 2.5–3 hours (allow 3+ hours if arriving Houston during rush hour — avoid 4–7 PM)
- **Fuel stops:**
  - **Buc-ee's in Luling, TX** (~55 miles east of Austin on I-10) — Highly recommended. Cleanest restrooms in America, incredible Texas BBQ, beaver nuggets (a Texas snack the kids will ask about for years). This is genuinely a road trip landmark.
  - If you need another stop, **Columbus, TX** (mile 102 on I-10) has a Flying J with good fuel prices
- **HOU vs. IAH:** Since your flight departs from HOU (Hobby), drop the car at **HOU airport** — it's closer and simpler. HOU is significantly smaller and less stressful than IAH.

### ⚠️ Budget Reality Check

**To stay under $3,000, you need to make deliberate choices:**

| If you choose... | 3-Night Hotel | 4-Night Hotel | Activities | Total Estimate |
|-----------------|---------------|---------------|------------|----------------|
| **Budget combo** | Hampton Inn (~$450) | Fairfield South (~$560) | Selective | ~$2,400–$2,600 ✅ |
| **Mid combo** | Drury Plaza (~$570) | Hyatt Place (~$760) | Moderate | ~$2,700–$2,900 ✅ |
| **Premium combo** | Drury Plaza (~$570) | South Congress Hotel (~$1,000) | Full schedule | ~$3,400–$3,600 ❌ |

### 💡 Top Cost-Cutting Tips
1. **The Drury Plaza free meals are your single best budget move** — a family of 4 eating free breakfast + evening food = ~$80–$100/day in savings
2. **Book SeaWorld/Six Flags online 2+ weeks out** — online advance pricing can be 40% cheaper than gate
3. **Lean into free Austin activities** — the bats, Zilker Park, Capitol, and SoCo walking are all free and genuinely among the best experiences
4. **Grocery run on arrival** — buy breakfast items, snacks, and drinks at an HEB (Texas's excellent regional grocery chain) to avoid convenience store pricing all week
5. **Skip the Houston activities** — if budget is tight, make April 17 a driving/rest day and skip Space Center Houston ($100+ for family)

## 7. 🧳 Practical Tips

### Best Apps for Road Trips with Kids

| App | Use |
|-----|-----|
| **GasBuddy** | Find cheapest gas along your route — can save $10–$15 on a Texas road trip |
| **Roadtrippers Plus** | Best overall road trip planning app — shows attractions, restaurants, and hotels along your route |
| **Waze** | Better than Google Maps for real-time traffic on Texas highways (especially I-35 through San Marcos) |
| **AllTrails** | For Enchanted Rock and any nature hikes — shows difficulty, reviews, trail maps |
| **Heads Up! (Ellen's Game)** | Car game — kids ages 8 & 11 will play this for hours |
| **Spotify / Audible** | Download a family audiobook before you leave. *The Lightning Thief* is perfect for ages 8–11 on a Texas road trip (Greek mythology + adventure) |

### What to Pack in the Car

**Kid Survival Kit:**
- [ ] Reusable water bottles (one per person — Texas in April can be 80°F+)
- [ ] Individual snack bags (pretzels, goldfish, granola bars, fruit pouches)
- [ ] Small backpack per kid with their own entertainment
- [ ] Portable charger / power bank
- [ ] Car phone mount (for navigation)
- [ ] Sunscreen (SPF 50 — Texas sun is serious)
- [ ] Hand sanitizer + small first aid kit
- [ ] Change of clothes per kid in an easily accessible bag (not buried in suitcase)
- [ ] Zip-lock bags (for wet swimsuits, snacks, car trash)
- [ ] Small cooler for drinks and snacks

**For the Drive:**
- [ ] Download offline maps on Google Maps/Waze before leaving (Texas highways have some dead zones)
- [ ] Headphone splitter or individual wireless earbuds for kids
- [ ] Activity books / Mad Libs (old school, kids still love them)

### 🎉 April Events & Festivals to Know About

#### San Antonio — April 10–13
> ⚠️ **CRITICAL:** **Fiesta San Antonio** typically runs in mid-to-late April (check exact dates for 2025 — it sometimes overlaps with Spring Break). Fiesta is a massive 10-day citywide festival that is *wonderful* for families (parades, food, music, lights on the Riverwalk) but also means **hotels are more expensive and the Riverwalk is extremely crowded**. Check the exact 2025 dates — if Fiesta starts during your stay, embrace it and experience it; if it starts the week after, your timing is actually ideal for smaller crowds.

#### Austin — April 13–17
- **Austin Reggae Festival** (Auditorium Shores, Lady Bird Lake) — typically first weekend of April, may catch the tail end; free/low-cost and very family friendly
- **SXSW** ends in mid-March, so you'll miss the chaos (good thing for families)
- **Texas Wildflowers** 🌸 — April is peak bluebonnet season. The highway medians and Hill Country roadsides will be carpeted in wildflowers. Stop for the obligatory Texas bluebonnet family photo on your way to/from Enchanted Rock — you'll see other families doing it too and will understand immediately why it's a Texas tradition.
